title: Compact code-render path for consumer list card faces
description: Analogue of Android wpass-tjc.2 (walt-passes-android PR #185, CompactCodeView + the list-face concession). The consumer wallet list renders a scannable card's actual code on its stack card face: QR as a ~66pt square tile, Code 128 as a full-width ~40pt band inside a white backing tile. Today this is impossible from outside the kernel: BarcodeRenderer (the CGImage-producing engine in Sources/UI/BarcodeView.swift) is internal, BarcodeView enforces gate-distance minimums (QR 240x240, 1D 320x96), ScannableCardView likewise, and ScannableCardTile's small preview (QR 96x96 / 1D 132x40) has fileprivate sizing. DELIVER: a public, size-parameterized compact render entry (mirror Android's CompactCodeView semantics - a SwiftUI view taking payload + format + target size/height) that renders QR and Code 128 at card-face scale, preserving quiet zones and white backing, explicitly documented as a recognition surface (NOT scannability-guaranteed - that is the detail surface's job; this is the 'list-face concession' from the Android ADR). Keep the gate-distance minimums on the existing detail views untouched. QR + Code 128 only (CoreImage encoders); other symbologies remain out of scope (ADR passes-ui-2). Follow the Android kernel PR #185 shape: study walt-passes-android's CompactCodeView API + tests and mirror naming/doc language where the platforms align. Include unit tests (render produces non-placeholder output at compact sizes for both formats; size parameterization respected; quiet-zone preserved).
notes: Implemented on branch ios-ipass-65p1-compact-code-render (worktree passes-ios-ipass-65p1), commit 0da089e: public CompactCodeView mirroring Android wpass-tjc.2 - white backing pinned, 8pt quiet zone, nearest-neighbor, compact floors QR 48x48 / 1D 96x32, unsupported symbologies route to failure tile not grey placeholder. 526 tests pass, swift-format + swiftlint strict clean. cole-branch-review: Merge (one non-blocking shared-pattern a11y verification noted: Color.clear failure-tile label, mirrors ScannableCardView - verify on device, fix both sites in follow-up if needed). security-review running.
close_reason: Merged via PR #41 (squash). Public CompactCodeView mirroring Android wpass-tjc.2: pinned white backing, quiet zone, compact floors below detail minimums, failure-tile routing for unsupported symbologies. 526 tests pass; security-review no findings; cole-branch-review Merge. Unblocks consumer bead ios-te9.5.

title: Kernel support for Walt iOS passes UI redesign (consumer epic in walt-ios)
description: Companion epic to the Walt iOS Passes UI redesign, the iOS port of Android consumer epic wlt-mx2d (approved Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/YZyPSjvEFmhDbPfk2poqmQ/26.07.13---Stacked--Scrollable-Passes) and the analogue of the Android kernel companion epic wpass-tjc (walt-passes-android, closed: PRs #184-#187). The Walt iOS list becomes an Apple-Wallet-style overlapping card stack with content-true card faces: scannable cards render their ACTUAL code on the list face (QR ~66pt tile, or full-width ~40pt Code 128 band on white backing) and PDF documents render a page-0 thumbnail. Detail surfaces get a paged PDF hero with next-page peek. Scope decisions (human-approved 2026-07-25): existing artifact types only (pkpass, PDF, scannable - no image/composite port), QR + Code 128 only (no new encoders in this epic). Most redesign work is consumer-side (walt-ios); the kernel gaps found by audit: (1) BarcodeRenderer is internal and BarcodeView/ScannableCardView hardcode gate-distance minimum sizes (QR 240x240, 1D 320x96), so there is no public size-parameterized compact render path for card faces - Android solved this with CompactCodeView (wpass-tjc.2 / PR #185); (2) the PDF pager with symmetric next-page peek needs PDFThumbnailCache capacity control + adjacent-page prefetch (Android: wpass-tjc.3 / PR #186, cache maxSize 7 vs default 5 - evicting a still-painted page bitmap would crash); (3) threat-model/ADR amendments for the new list-surface presentation (actual codes + page renders on list faces; the compact-render list-face concession) - Android: wpass-tjc.4 / PR #187. NOT needed on iOS (already present, verified): document rename updateDocumentLabel (wpass-tjc.1 analogue), public paged renderer PDFRendererBinder.probe/render, issuer PassColors parsing. Unlike Android, document rename shipped with the original iOS port.
close_reason: All three children shipped: PR #41 (CompactCodeView compact render path), #42 (pager audit ADR - no kernel change needed), #43 (list-surface posture ADR). Consumer epic ios-te9 can now build against the kernel surface.

title: Threat-model + ADR amendments for redesigned list surfaces
description: Analogue of Android wpass-tjc.4 (walt-passes-android PR #187, ADR/threat-model amendments). The consumer redesign changes what kernel-rendered untrusted content appears WHERE: actual barcode renders and PDF page-0 thumbnails now appear on wallet LIST card faces (previously detail-only), a compact code-render path exists whose output is explicitly not scannability-guaranteed (the list-face concession), and the consumer detail surface composes kernel BarcodeView inside a consumer-built card rather than kernel PassFront (trust captions become consumer-owned text). Amend the kernel threat model + ADRs to record: (1) list-face rendering of untrusted content still flows exclusively through the kernel's bounded decode paths (BoundedImage-equivalent guards, isolated PDF rasterization) - enumerate the invariants a consumer must uphold; (2) the compact-render concession and why quiet-zone/white-backing are still enforced at small sizes; (3) the trust-presentation boundary: which trust signals the kernel guarantees non-suppressibly (ExpiredOverlay inside PassFront, ScannableCardScreen provenance caption) vs which the consumer now owns when composing primitives directly, and what the consumer contract is (mirror the language Android PR #187 settled on). Read walt-passes-android's merged amendments first and port the reasoning, not just the text - flag any iOS-specific divergence (e.g. no isolated-process renderer on iOS; Data Protection instead) explicitly. Docs-only bead; no code.
close_reason: Merged via PR #43 (squash): ADR passes-ui-6 ports wpass-tjc.4 reasoning (issuer color pkpass-only, content-true previews on existing bounded paths, no verified affordance at list scale) and makes the kernel/consumer trust-presentation boundary explicit for consumers composing BarcodeView directly. security-review: no findings. cole-branch-review: Merge.

title: PDF pager support: thumbnail cache capacity + adjacent-page prefetch
description: Analogue of Android wpass-tjc.3 (walt-passes-android PR #186, pager adjacent-page prefetch). The redesigned consumer document detail is a horizontal pager with a symmetric next/previous-page peek (~56pt insets) and an n/N pill; each page is a kernel-rasterized thumbnail. Android found the kernel cache default too small for the peek window: with beyondViewportPageCount=1 the pager can hold up to ~5 live page bitmaps plus prefetch, and evicting a still-painted bitmap crashes - they exposed cache capacity (consumer passes maxSize 7) and added adjacent-page prefetch. AUDIT the iOS kernel's PassesPDFUI surface (PDFThumbnail.swift: PDFThumbnailState, PageImageHandle, PDFThumbnailCache, PDFThumbnailViewModel.start/stop, ThumbnailRenderTarget/Context) against those needs: (1) is PDFThumbnailCache capacity configurable by the consumer? (2) can the consumer warm/prefetch adjacent pages without visible jank when swiping? (3) are handles safe against eviction-while-displayed (iOS may already be safe if PageImageHandle retains its CGImage - verify and document)? Implement whatever is missing, mirroring the Android PR #186 API shape where it fits Swift. If the audit finds iOS already safe and sufficient, close this bead with the audit written up in the close reason and an ADR note - a no-op outcome is acceptable.
close_reason: Audit complete, no kernel change needed - landed as ADR passes-pdf-ui-6 via PR #42 (squash). (1) PDFThumbnailCache(maxSize:) already public, consumer passes 7. (2) Eviction cannot invalidate a displayed page: no-op onEvict + strong CGImage-backed PageImageHandle; Android's recycle crash class structurally absent under ARC. (3) Peek prefetch works through existing public PDFThumbnailViewModel + shared lock-guarded cache; no speculative API added. security-review: no findings. cole-branch-review: Merge.

title: CI cost tiering: add Linux swift-format/SwiftLint cheap gate so macOS drops off the per-PR path
description: Follow-up to the ci.yml cost change (PR-gate macOS + weekly cron, dropped post-merge run, added concurrency/timeout). GOAL: take the 10x macOS build/test off the every-PR critical path by adding a 1x Linux cheap tier (swift-format lint + SwiftLint) that gates auto-merge, mirroring the iOS app repo's CHEAP/FULL tiering. BLOCKERS found 2026-06-25: (1) PassesCore imports Apple Compression -> kernel targets do NOT build on Linux, so the cheap tier can only LINT (syntactic), not compile. (2) Kernel has ~685 swift-format violations vs the app's .swift-format config and was never linted; SwiftLint app config needs its included: paths adapted to the kernel layout. PLAN: on a branch, (a) copy app .swift-format + .swiftlint.yml, adapt paths, (b) swift-format format --in-place + resolve SwiftLint, verify swift build/test still pass on macOS, (c) restructure ci.yml: Linux lint job (every PR, gates auto-merge) + macOS build/test moved to FULL (workflow_dispatch + weekly cron + full-ci label, draft-until-green for risky signature/parsing changes). NOTE: lint-only gating reduces merge safety on this security-critical kernel vs today's macOS-gated merges; the full-ci label/draft flow covers risky PRs. Do NOT commit the 685-line reformat straight to main.
close_reason: Merged via PR #33 (squash f5d6a74). Cheap Linux lint tier gates auto-merge; macOS build/test moved to full-ci.yml. Auto-merge validated the new pipeline end-to-end on the PR.

title: 1D symbology encoders: EAN-13, UPC-A, Code 39 (unblocks full format-chip parity with Android)
description: Deliberately OUTSIDE the redesign epic ipass-65p (human scope decision 2026-07-25: redesigned create form ships with QR + Code 128 chips only). Android's redesigned create-code form offers QR / Code 128 / EAN-13 / UPC-A / Code 39; the iOS kernel renders only QR + Code 128 because CoreImage has no generators for the other three - they currently draw a grey placeholder (ADR passes-ui-2), which is why the consumer form hides them. DELIVER: kernel-native encoders for EAN-13, UPC-A, and Code 39 (module patterns are simple and well-specified; implement from the specs or port walt-passes-android's BarcodeEncoder, do NOT add a third-party dependency without escalation), wired into BarcodeRenderer + BarcodeView + the compact render path, with checksum validation on input, golden-pattern unit tests per symbology, and removal of the placeholder arm. Security-sensitive rendering of user-supplied payloads: keep input validation strict (charset + length per symbology) and escalate per section 7 if any design question arises. When this lands, file a consumer bead to add the three chips to the create form.
